paper_metadata.title: Achieving superior high-temperature strength and ductility in near-α titanium alloys by in-situ silicide modulation

evidence.quote: a novel in-situ silicide modulation strategy is proposed to achieve superior high-temperature strength and ductility synergy in near-α Ti alloys.

To ensure uniform distribution of Si powder on the surface of the TA15 powder, ball milling was conducted at 150 r min−1 for 10 h, using a ball-to-powder ratio of 2:1

parameters.cooling_method: average cooling rate approx. 120 °C min-1 to RT

evidence.quote: After ball milling, the mixed powders were loaded into a 40 mm diameter graphite mold and sintered utilizing an SPS ma- chine (HPD25, FCT Systeme). The SPS sintering was performed at 1200 °C for 10 min under a vacuum with an applied pressure of 35 MPa. Following the sintering stage, the average cooling rate from the sintering temperature to RT was approximately 120 °C min−1 .
